prospect.name: Kitch Cash
prospect.location: Rural eastern United States, Central time zone; phone area code 615 suggests the Nashville area
prospect.occupation: Camera operator in live music video production — works handheld wireless camera on stage at concerts and festivals, feeding the big screens. Holds a roughly 30lb camera for an hour and a half at a time. Tours seasonally in spring and autumn, typically 15 to 40 shows with three or four show nights a week, living on a tour bus.
prospect.family_status: Has a girlfriend, who he credits with prompting his interest in paying attention to how food affects him. No children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete, primarily baseball. Started traditional weight-room training in late middle school and describes the weight room as where he grew most. Won a baseball scholarship and played one year in college before quitting because his body was hurting — 'I was strong, but just couldn't move.' Took a couple of years off entirely, then four or five years of intermittent stints with jump rope, kettlebells, running and some yoga. For roughly the past month to six weeks has been doing Trevor's YouTube kettlebell workouts almost daily. Prefers to train outdoors, barefoot in grass, without music or screens. Also practising rope flow. Job itself is physically demanding and he describes it as an endurance activity.
prospect.medical: No conditions were asked about and none were disclosed as diagnoses. Volunteered in passing that his back was 'not working great' after his baseball years and that his low back is 'the first thing to go', plus a wish for more hip flexibility and a stronger core. Reports sleep was erratic and mood was fluctuating widely before he resumed training, and that both improved markedly within one to two weeks of starting kettlebell work. Notes starch makes him bloated and excess sugar makes him feel poor. No injury screening question was ever asked on this call.

signals: Explicit and unusually articulate statement of lost ground — 'I did lose respect for myself in the last four or five years because it didn't take care of myself very well... I really took my hands off the reins'
Former athlete whose body stopped working for him and who walked away from it entirely, now returning
Carries visible regret and named the turning point himself: 'I just remember having this moment of like, I don't, I want to respect that guy. And I don't right now'
What he wants back is character rather than physique — 'we're not doing this for abs. That might be a side effect, but we're not doing this for abs'
DISTINCTION FROM the_optimizer: he is not already fit and successful buying an upgrade; the purchase is a self-repair project with a fitness vehicle
Unusual for a rebuilder in that he has already restarted unaided and is getting results from free content, so he is buying structure and supervision rather than a way back in

objections.raw_quote: I, because I've been taking the summer off, and I haven't had income since May, I feel more drawn to being able to finance it, or draw it out, or even make a couple of payments. That feels more comfortable to me.
objections.rep_response: Offered three structures in sequence — in-house three payments of $2,000 with no interest, in-house six payments of $1,200 with interest, and third-party Payva financing over up to 12 months at roughly $650 — then asked for his credit score. The prospect chose the interest-free three-pay immediately.

objections.raw_quote: what is his approach to alcohol like I'm curious... I'm curious like what his take is on no alcohol during the six months
objections.rep_response: Answered honestly that nothing is prohibited — 'he cannot prohibit anything, right' — then gave his own position, ten years without drinking, and a nutritional rationale: empty calories, and that current evidence indicates no safe amount. Closed with a permissive caveat about a glass of wine every couple of weeks.

objections.raw_quote: usually when I go on the road, like that's all I'm eating completely catered food that I don't have control over... from September through December, will be on the road, which will make four or five days a week will make my dieting pretty specific.
objections.rep_response: Said he would receive guidelines for choosing when not eating at home, and suggested sourcing his own food near where he is stationed rather than eating the catered meals. Did not address the days where that is not possible.

notable.note: The most emotionally substantive discovery in the batch, produced by a single question. When the prospect said he had lost respect for himself, the rep stopped and asked 'why would you say that? It's a powerful word to use' — and got a two-minute self-diagnosis that named the exact gap the product sells against. The reflect-back that followed was equally good: 'you're on a journey right now that you don't need motivation to actually do it. It's more of a structure how to do it.' Set against that, the physical baseline is the thinnest in the batch — no age, no height, no weight, and no injury question was asked at all, despite the prospect twice volunteering low back problems and working a job that has him holding 30lb at height for ninety minutes. Two commercial points worth escalating: the prospect is already getting real results from the free YouTube content ('my sleep has gotten immensely better. Literally within a week and a half'), which is an unaddressed reason not to buy; and he disclosed no income since May while agreeing to two $2,000 payments before his September income resumes.
